title: Bootstrap CDK and create a GitHub deploy role in each chatticus-* account
description:
Ryan (2026-09-30): set up the same CI/CD in the new per-environment accounts: CI in GitHub Actions, CD by CDK deploy through GitHub OIDC. This card is the foundation and needs no DNS or data decisions.

## Findings (read-only, 2026-09-30)
- chatticus-development, -staging and -production are empty: no CDKToolkit stack, no OIDC provider, no stacks. Non-root SSO sessions (AdministratorAccess) work for all three.
- infra/lib/github-deploy-stack.ts cannot be reused as is: it IMPORTS the GitHub OIDC provider (fromOpenIdConnectProviderArn, which must already exist) and creates all three environment roles in ONE account. A new account needs the provider created and only its own environment's role.
- Trust is by the OIDC sub claim pinned to the repo's immutable owner/repo ids plus environment:NAME (see the long comment in that file); keep that, it was root-caused once already.
- The CDK account is chosen from the credentials (CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT in bin/chatticus.ts), so deploying to a different account needs no code change: a workflow's AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN environment secret decides where it deploys. That secret is therefore the cutover switch, not something to change early.

## Plan
1. cdk bootstrap aws://ACCOUNT/us-east-1 in each account (AGENTS.md allows bootstrap and deploy as the only AWS writes).
2. A stack that creates the OIDC provider (one per account) and ONE deploy role trusting environment:<that account's environment> only, with a test that asserts the trust, and the legacy stack left untouched until legacy is retired. Deploy it once per account locally with the SSO profile (the documented one-time path).
3. Do NOT change any AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN secret here; workflows keep deploying to legacy until the cutover card.

## Done when
In each account: CDKToolkit is CREATE_COMPLETE, the deploy role exists, and a dispatch of a no-op check (sts get-caller-identity through OIDC from GitHub Actions) succeeds without touching legacy.
